description: We’re space and tech enthusiasts taking on “Abandoned but not Forgotten,” telling the story of the rovers and probes NASA left on the Moon and Mars for school-age space fans. We’re looking for teammates skilled in writing, graphic design or video editing, web development, or NASA data research. No expertise required, just curiosity and enthusiasm. Join us!
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive field guide for ages 10 to 15 that tells the stories of 11 pieces of NASA hardware left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space, including Eagle, the lunar rovers, Ingenuity, Voyager 1 and Pioneer 10. Visitors pick an object from a list or a map, read a short story and answer a quiz question. It addresses the challenge by telling what each object was, what it did and what happened to it, with each fact labelled Confirmed, Scientific explanation, Engineers think or Still unknown, and every story linking to its sources. These objects are part of space history, and the guide helps young people learn it while telling facts from open questions.
details:
What it does and how it works. Abandoned but Not Forgotten is a single web page. A visitor picks one of 11 objects from a list or from a Moon or Mars map, or filters by Moon, Mars or deep space. Each object opens a story told in short chapters, with a credited NASA image where we found one, and ends with a quiz question. The 11 objects are Eagle, the lunar rovers, ALSEP, Surveyor 3 and the Apollo 14 golf balls on the Moon; Spirit and Opportunity, Ingenuity, Viking 1 and Sojourner on Mars; and Voyager 1 and Pioneer 10 in deep space.

Benefits and intended impact. The guide gives young people a clear, friendly way to learn about spacecraft and equipment left behind, and to see which parts of each story are known and which are not. Each fact is labelled Confirmed, Scientific explanation, Engineers think or Still unknown, and every story links to its sources, so readers can check for themselves.

Tools. We built it with HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file, with SVG maps and the Poppins font. It is hosted free on GitHub Pages, so it needs no sign-up. We used Claude, an AI assistant, to help draft the code.

What is creative. We turned abandoned hardware into stories for ages 10 to 15, and added deep-space objects so the guide goes beyond the Moon and Mars. Labelling the open mysteries is part of the design.

What we considered. We checked every date and claim against NASA pages and linked them. We used only images with a verified credit, and left out three photos where the credit was unclear. We also kept the text short and plain for the age group, and used a dark theme with light text for readability.
